question.value: Characterize the multiphase gas (ionized atomic, warm and cold molecular) kinematics, morphology, physical conditions, and energetics in the circumnuclear region of NGC 1365 to understand AGN feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution.

evidence.quote: Specifically, we combined spatially resolved spectroscopic data from JWST/MIRI, VLT/MUSE, and ALMA to provide a multiphase characterization of the ionized atomic and the warm and cold molecular gas phases.

In particular, it allows for a detailed characterization of the kinematics, morphology, and energetics of the circumnuclear environment in NGC 1365, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of AGN feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution.

analysis_steps.goal: Model optical and mid-IR line fluxes with HOMERUN and kinematic outflow structure with MOKA3D to derive outflow mass and energetics

method.value: Fit 60 optical+mid-IR emission lines in the 1.5" radius aperture using HOMERUN (combining dust-free AGN and dusty SF CLOUDY model grids) to derive ionized gas masses, and fit [Ne V]14um and [O III]5007A cubes with MOKA3D to obtain deprojected outflow velocities and energetics.

evidence.quote: We fit the fluxes of 60 ionized and neutral atomic emission lines measured from the MIRI and MUSE spectra (32 from MIRI and 28 from MUSE, see Figs. 2 and 9) extracted within a 1.5 radius aperture centered on the outflow region (see Fig. 6).

We inferred the [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ and [O III]$\lambda 5007\text{\AA}$ intrinsic (i.e., de-projected) radial velocities of the outflow (v$_\mathrm{out}$) using the 3D multicloud $\mathrm{MOKA^{3D}}$ kinematic model (cite: Marconcini2023).

assumptions.value: Outflowing gas is fully ionized by the AGN (dust-free AGN clouds, dusty SF clouds with equal metallicity); constant flux density over time in each spaxel

evidence.loc: Model grids of AGNs and SF
evidence.quote: Both components were assumed to have the same metallicity; however, while we adopted dust-free models for the AGN component, we included dust in the SF models and corrected gas-phase metallicities using the depletion factors listed in Table 7.8 of Hazy 1 (Cloudy v23.1).

In this way, under the assumption that the outflowing gas is fully ionized by the AGN, we avoided including the contribution from systemic or SF-related components, ensuring that the derived masses trace the outflowing gas itself.

fitting.value: Non-negative least squares without regularization in HOMERUN minimizing reduced-chi2 loss function L_min; 3D spaxel-by-spaxel kinematic fitting in MOKA3D

evidence.quote: This is achieved by solving a non-negative least squares problem, whereby the weights of each cloud are constrained to be non-negative.
This loss function is effectively a reduced $\chi^2$ statistic, so values $\lesssim 1$ indicate a statistically good fit.

validation.value: Majority of 60 lines reproduced within 15% accuracy (L_min = 0.6); MOKA3D reproduces observed moment maps with discrepancies below 5%

evidence.quote: The unique approach of HOMERUN enables us to reproduce at the same time 60 different emission lines in different ionization stages, with the majority of them reproduced with better than 15$\%$ accuracy.

With $\mathrm{MOKA^{3D}}$ we reproduce the line emission on a spaxel-by-spaxel basis, which as a consequence guarantee that the model reproduces the observed moment maps, with discrepancies between observed and modeled moment maps below 5$\%$.

findings_qualitative.value: Cold molecular gas (CO 3-2) and warm molecular gas (H2 pure-rotational lines) trace the rotating circumnuclear ring and stellar disk without evidence of a molecular outflow.

evidence.quote: The cold molecular gas traced by the CO(3-2) transition shares the same ordered kinematics of the stellar galaxy disk (cite: Venturi_2018), with no evidence of outflowing material.

The same conclusion holds for the warm molecular gas traced by the H$_2$ pure-rotational transitions, with the exception of a peculiar high-$\sigma$ unresolved region located southward of the nucleus.

findings_qualitative.value: Ionized gas morphology and kinematics stratify by ionization potential: low-IP (<25 eV) species trace the rotating disk and circumnuclear ring, while high-IP (>54 eV) species trace the bipolar outflow including the dust-obscured NW receding counter-cone.

evidence.quote: Low-IP species ($\leq$ 25 eV) mainly trace the rotating disk, while higher-IP species (up to $\sim$120 eV) trace the outflowing gas.

The [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ emission also reveals the NW receding counterpart of the ionization cone, which is undetected in [O III]$\lambda 5007\text{\AA}$ due to large extinction caused by the galaxy disk at optical wavelengths.

findings_qualitative.value: Mid-IR diagnostic diagrams penetrate central dust obscuration to reveal AGN ionization at the nucleus and shock/AGN interaction zones at the edge of the circumnuclear ring, whereas optical BPT diagrams at the nucleus appear SF-dominated due to dust extinction.

evidence.loc: Resolved diagnostic diagrams for gas excitation
evidence.quote: In the nuclear region, the optical BPT appears to be dominated by SF due to strong dust obscuration, as is indicated by the Balmer decrement (see Appendix 9 and Fig. 12). In contrast, mid-IR diagnostics can penetrate the dust screen and clearly reveal AGN ionization at the nucleus.

claims.hypothesis: Cold and warm molecular gas and ionized gas species across different ionization potentials trace distinct kinematic components (rotating disk vs. bipolar AGN outflow) in the circumnuclear region of NGC 1365.
claims.experiment: Fit emission lines spaxel-by-spaxel in JWST/MIRI MRS, VLT/MUSE, and ALMA CO(3-2) datacubes to produce moment maps and velocity channel maps across gas phases and ionization potentials.
claims.result: CO(3-2), H2 0-0 S(1)-S(7), and low-IP (<25 eV) ionized lines follow stellar disk rotation (~110-120 km s^-1) in the circumnuclear ring, while high-IP (>54 eV) lines like [Ne V]14um trace the SE-NW bipolar outflow (up to -120/+100 km s^-1, sigma up to ~170 km s^-1) and reveal the obscured NW receding cone.
claims.finding: Molecular and low-IP ionized gas trace the rotating disk with no molecular outflow in the circumnuclear region, whereas high-IP ionized species trace the AGN-driven biconical outflow through the dust.

evidence.quote: Moment maps show that both cold and warm molecular gas trace the circumnuclear ring, following the rotation of the stellar disk.
Low-IP species ($\leq$ 25 eV) mainly trace the rotating disk, while higher-IP species (up to $\sim$120 eV) trace the outflowing gas.
The cold molecular gas traced by the CO(3-2) transition shares the same ordered kinematics of the stellar galaxy disk (cite: Venturi_2018), with no evidence of outflowing material.

claims.hypothesis: Spatially resolved mid-IR line ratios can penetrate nuclear dust obscuration in NGC 1365 to reveal the true ionizing mechanism and gas density compared to optical diagnostics.
claims.experiment: Construct PSF-matched mid-IR diagnostic diagrams ([O IV]/[Ne II], [Ne III]/[Ne II], [Ne V]/[Ne II]) and compare with optical MUSE BPT diagrams; compute electron densities from [Ne V]24um/14um and [S II]6716/6731 using PyNeb.
claims.result: Mid-IR diagnostic maps show AGN and shock/AGN excitation in the central region where optical BPT diagrams appear SF-dominated (with A_V up to 3.7 mag); [Ne V]24um/14um yields n_e = (750 +/- 440) cm^-3 in the outflow aperture compared to (350 +/- 40) cm^-3 from [S II].
claims.finding: Mid-IR diagnostics penetrate the nuclear dust screen to reveal central AGN ionization and denser gas closer to the AGN that are obscured or diluted in optical tracers.

evidence.quote: Unlike optical diagnostics, spatially resolved mid-IR diagnostics reveal the key role of the active galactic nucleus (AGN) as the source of gas ionization in the central region.
From the mid-IR [Ne V] line ratio, we estimate an electron density of (750$\pm$440) cm$^{-3}$, while from the [S II] lines we find a consistent value of (350$\pm$40) cm$^{-3}$.

claims.hypothesis: Combining multicloud photoionization modeling (HOMERUN) with 3D kinematic modeling (MOKA3D) overcomes the inconsistencies of classical single-density/single-ionization outflow mass and energetics estimates.
claims.experiment: Simultaneously fit 60 optical and mid-IR emission lines in a 1.5" aperture with HOMERUN and fit 3D outflow kinematics of [Ne V]14um and [O III]5007A with MOKA3D, comparing derived outflow masses and rates against the classical method.
claims.result: HOMERUN+MOKA3D yields consistent ionized outflow masses (M_[Ne V] = 109 +/- 2 x 10^3 M_sun, M_[O III] = 88 +/- 9 x 10^3 M_sun) and mass outflow rates (~0.17 M_sun yr^-1) for both tracers, whereas the classical method gives discrepant masses by a factor of ~75 between [Ne V] (2.6 x 10^3 M_sun) and [O III] (20 x 10^4 M_sun).
claims.finding: Self-consistent multicloud photoionization and 3D kinematic modeling reconciles optical and mid-IR outflow tracers and shows that classical methods severely underestimate outflow masses for high-ionization species like [Ne V].

evidence.quote: The reliability of the more complex HOMERUN approach is demonstrated by the fact that classical method mass estimates differ by a factor of $\sim$75 between different tracers, highlighting the inherent inconsistencies of the traditional approach.

From HOMERUN, we calculated consistent mass outflow rates for [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ and [O III]$\lambda 5007\text{\AA}$, namely $\dot{\rm M}_{[Ne~V]}$ = $\left(1.72~\pm~0.20\right)~\times~10^{-1}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ and $\dot{\rm M}_{[O~III]}$ = $\left(1.68~\pm~0.31\right)~\times~10^{-1}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, respectively.

why_this_data.value: Combining JWST/MIRI MRS, VLT/MUSE, and ALMA ~0.30" CO(3-2) data traces ionized atomic, warm molecular, and cold molecular gas at matched spatial resolution across obscured nuclear regions.

evidence.quote: For NGC 1365, we combined data from the Medium-Resolution Spectrometer (MRS; (cite: Rieke2015; Labiano_21)) of MIRI with integral-field optical spectroscopy from VLT/MUSE and millimeter observations from ALMA.
In this work, we use the observations with resolution $\sim0.30$ corresponding to 30 pc, which better match the MIRI MRS spatial resolution and provide a maximum recoverable scale of 2.9.

why_this_method.value: HOMERUN+MOKA3D self-consistently decomposes superposed AGN and SF ionization components across 60 lines without assuming fixed ionization fractions or single densities, while 3D kinematic modeling accounts for outflow geometry and projection.

evidence.quote: Lastly, we applied, for the first time, a fully self-consistent combination of state-of-the-art photoionization and kinematic models (HOMERUN+$\mathrm{MOKA^{3D}}$) to estimate the intrinsic physical outflow properties, kinematics, and energetics - overcoming the limitations of classical methods based on oversimplified assumptions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CO(1-0) molecular outflow interpretation by Gao et al. (2021) is rejected in favor of noncircular bar-driven inflowing motions

evidence.quote: This finding, which is consistent with the lack of any molecular outflow in the circumnuclear region (cite: Combes_2019), is in contrast to the CO (1-0) wind reported by (cite: Gao2021).

Their outflow interpretation was based on velocity residuals from a rotating disk model on larger spatial scales, which resemble those observed in H$\alpha$ and are more likely due to noncircular inflowing motions along the bar (see their Fig. 6).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Shock photoionization models were excluded from the HOMERUN multiline fitting because photoionizing shocks are inefficient in powering AGN narrow-line emission and shock grids largely overlap with AGN and SF grids

evidence.loc: Resolved diagnostic diagrams for gas excitation
evidence.quote: However, (cite: Laor1998) showed that photoionizing shocks are extremely inefficient in powering the narrow line emission in AGNs.

evidence.loc: Resolved diagnostic diagrams for gas excitation
evidence.quote: For these reasons, in Section 3.5 we consider only AGN and SF grids to model the optical and mid-IR emission lines.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Nuclear torus differential IR extinction explanation by Dudik et al. (2007) for [Ne V] ratios in the low-density limit is ruled out in favor of Spitzer/IRS aperture loss effects

evidence.quote: Exploiting the spatially resolved [Ne V] emission in our data and the density values in the nuclear region, we can rule out this interpretation.

This means that the SH module surely lost part of the [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ flux, leading to an artificially enhancement of the [Ne V]$\lambda 24\mu\mathrm{m}$/[Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ line ratio.

limitations_admitted.value: MIRI Ch3 FoV includes some AGN-illuminated disk gas not part of the outflow, though all gas in the ionization cone is assumed to be outflowing in the analysis.

evidence.quote: Although in this analysis we focus on the FoV of Ch3, which also includes a fraction of disk gas illuminated by the AGN and not part of the outflow, it would be more accurate to refer to this region as the ionization cone rather than calling it outflow. However, we will assume in the following that all the gas in the ionization cone is in outflow.

limitations_admitted.value: Strong nuclear continuum emission dominates the spectra at the galaxy nucleus, causing an apparent lack of line emission in some moment maps.

evidence.quote: Note that while some lines appear to lack emission in the nuclear region of the galaxy in the moment maps, this is because the spectra are dominated by strong continuum emission rather than a genuine absence of emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Low S/N of mid-IR hydrogen recombination lines (Pf-alpha and Hu-alpha) prevents deriving a spatially resolved extinction map directly from the mid-IR spectra.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, in our data the S/N of the Pf$\alpha$ and Hu$\alpha$ (i.e., H I (6−5) at 7.46 $\mu$m and H I (7−6) at 12.37 $\mu$m, respectively) is too low to derive a reliable extinction map directly from the mid-IR spectra.

limitations_admitted.value: HOMERUN mass-luminosity scaling relations derived for NGC 1365 are customized to its specific physical conditions and are not universally applicable to other AGNs without dedicated fitting.

evidence.quote: They are derived specifically from the HOMERUN multicloud modeling customized for the physical conditions and emission properties of NGC 1365. Therefore, applying these relations to other galaxies requires performing a dedicated HOMERUN fit

referee_caveats_inferred: Assuming all AGN-ionized gas within the 1.5 arcsec aperture is outflowing (rather than partially systemic illuminated disk gas) may overestimate the total outflowing mass and energetics.
The HOMERUN modeling is performed on an integrated 1.5 arcsec radius aperture rather than spaxel-by-spaxel, whereas MOKA3D kinematics are fit spaxel-by-spaxel.
